clauses.label: operative lead
clauses.text:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the Federal Vacancies Reform 
Act of 1998, 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq., it is hereby ordered that:

clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Order of Succession. Subject to the provisions of section 2 of 
this order, the following officers, in the order listed, shall act as and perform 
the functions and duties of the office of Attorney General, during any period 
in which the Attorney General, the Deputy Attorney General, the Associate 
Attorney General, and any officers designated by the Attorney General pursu-
ant to 28 U.S.C. 508 to act as Attorney General have died, resigned, or 
otherwise become unable to perform the functions and duties of the office 
of Attorney General, until such time as at least one of the officers mentioned 
above is able to perform the functions and duties of that office:

clauses.label: (a)
clauses.text: (a) United States Attorney for the District of Columbia;

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text: (b) United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois; and

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text: (c) United States Attorney for the Central District of California.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Exceptions. (a) No individual who is serving in an office listed 
in section 1 of this order in an acting capacity, by virtue of so serving, 
shall act as Attorney General pursuant to this order.

clauses.label: (b)
clauses.text:
(b) No individual listed in section 1 shall act as Attorney General unless 
that individual is otherwise eligible to so serve under the Federal Vacancies 
Reform Act of 1998.

clauses.label: (c)
clauses.text:
(c) Notwithstanding the provisions of this order, the President retains 
discretion, to the extent permitted by law, to depart from this order in 
designating an acting Attorney General.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. Executive Order 13557 of November 4, 2010, is revoked.

Executive Order 13762 of January 13, 2017 
Providing an Order of Succession Within the Department of 
Justice 
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the 
laws of the United States of America, including the Federal Vacancies Reform 
Act of 1998, 5 U.S.C. 3345 et seq., it is hereby ordered that: 
Section 1. Order of Succession. Subject to the provisions of section 2 of 
this order, the following officers, in the order listed, shall act as and perform 
the functions and duties of the office of Attorney General, during any period 
in which the Attorney General, the Deputy Attorney General, the Associate 
Attorney General, and any officers designated by the Attorney General pursu-
ant to 28 U.S.C. 508 to act as Attorney General have died, resigned, or 
otherwise become unable to perform the functions and duties of the office 
of Attorney General, until such time as at least one of the officers mentioned 
above is able to perform the functions and duties of that office: 
(a) United States Attorney for the District of Columbia; 
(b) United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois; and 
(c) United States Attorney for the Central District of California. 
Sec. 2. Exceptions. (a) No individual who is serving in an office listed 
in section 1 of this order in an acting capacity, by virtue of so serving, 
shall act as Attorney General pursuant to this order. 
(b) No individual listed in section 1 shall act as Attorney General unless 
that individual is otherwise eligible to so serve under the Federal Vacancies 
Reform Act of 1998. 
(c) Notwithstanding the provisions of this order, the President retains 
discretion, to the extent permitted by law, to depart from this order in 
designating an acting Attorney General. 
Sec. 3. Executive Order 13557 of November 4, 2010, is revoked.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 13762 (82 FR 7619, Jan. 19, 2017, signed Jan. 13, 2017): an order of succession within the Department of Justice (acting Attorney General: the U.S. Attorneys for D.C., N.D. Ill. and C.D. Cal.), with sec. 3 revoking EO 13557; no own term. I read the held full text of EO 13775 (82 FR 10697, Feb. 14, 2017, signed Feb. 9, 2017): it sets a new order of succession and sec. 3 'Revocation of Executive Order. Executive Order 13762 of January 13, 2017, is revoked.' That names EO 13762 by number and number-and-date, covers the whole order, has no exception or savings clause, and EO 13762 has no part that survives. D6 self-check: the later events are EO 13775 itself and EO 13787 (82 FR 16723, Apr. 5, 2017, signed Mar. 31, 2017), whose sec. 3 revokes EO 13775 and sets a new succession list; I read EO 13787 in full and it contains no wording reviving, restoring or re-adopting EO 13762 or EO 13557, so the revocation of the revoking order does not bring EO 13762 back. The other held texts that contain the number 13762 (EO 11501-11503, 12993) are hash or page-number noise. The OFR note 'Revoked by: EO 13775, February 9, 2017' agrees but is a lead only. Provisional NO hypothesis; effective date of the revocation (on signing, Feb. 9, 2017) is not otherwise adjudicated.
